findings: The sole change resolves the existing public codex_sandboxing::find_system_bwrap_in_path in the parent test process before the new shim is created; the existing cargo_bin("bwrap") remains the None fallback.

The existing exec-server package already depends on codex-sandboxing, and its public re-export is available under target_os=linux. Both helper callers are Linux-gated. This candidate needs no manifest or new dependency change.

Both callers resolve/write the helper before constructing the child-only PATH. exec_server_with_env applies Command::envs to the child without mutating the parent PATH. The newly written shim cannot recursively select itself through this ordering.

Full original shim text is byte-identical: help and capability probes delegate to the resolved executable, fail-once/logging semantics remain, original namespace/argv0 arguments and inherited descriptors pass unchanged through exec.

The helper's PATH discovery is not itself the full product capability-selection function. The existing product still checks the shim's delegated help and retains its fallback/unsupported behavior. This audit does not assert that every host system bwrap is supported or that an unsupported system binary now becomes acceptable.
The original grouping/fallback-count/PATH/permission tests and all their assertion bytes are outside the patch. Native validation and any separately authorized host probe remain pending.
